pillars.title: The Kelburn Recovery Centre Location
pillars.body: Kelburn Recovery Centre is located 7 kilometers south of Winnipeg on 45 beautiful acres along the Red River. The center offers a 10,000 square-foot residential home with 10 bedrooms, allowing clients to share a bedroom with one other roommate. The property provides numerous activities like the 9-hole PGA standard golf course, indoor swimming pool, sauna, and recreation room. The outdoor property comprises beautiful lakes and seasoned walking paths used for cross-country skiing in the winter and peaceful strolls in the summer.

pillars.title: Aftercare From the First Week, Then a Year of Check-ins
pillars.body: Kelburn started aftercare planning in a client's first week. Recovery coaches helped people find and apply for programs back home, and staff kept in regular contact for the first year after discharge. Alumni met at Kelburn on Thursday evenings and Saturday afternoons, in person or on Zoom, and the centre pointed graduates to Winnipeg sober living homes such as Two Ten Recovery, Destiny House and Riverwood House. Staff who ran these services were laid off when the centre closed in October 2025, so confirm with the owner before you count on any of them.

pillars.title: Support Services
pillars.body: Kelburn Recovery Centre offers a range of support services to ensure that clients receive the best possible care. The center provides medically assisted detox services, interventions services, residential care, and outpatient services. Clients also benefit from a team of experienced healthcare professionals, including certified addiction counselors, licensed psychologists, psychiatrists, and medical doctors. Additionally, Kelburn Recovery Centre offers comprehensive aftercare services designed to help clients achieve long-term recovery.

overview: The New Kelburn Recovery Centre is a premier rehabilitation facility located in Southern Manitoba, Canada. Under new ownership since October of 2021, the center offers inpatient treatment programs that start at 42 days and include a range of comprehensive services aimed at achieving successful levels of personal, social, and occupational functioning. With a certified team of professionals, including doctors, nurses, psychotherapists, clinical counselors, a registered massage therapist, a knowledge keeper, a master fitness trainer, and a red seal chef, clients can rest assured they are receiving the highest level of care.

The New Kelburn Recovery Centre is committed to providing responsible and evidence-based treatment practices in a professional and affordable manner. Their multidisciplinary approach to recovery focuses on teaching constructive life skills as a means of discontinuing harmful or self-limiting behavior. With medically assisted detox, psychiatric assessments, customized therapy, and after-care support, their programs are tailored to meet the individual needs of clients. Overall, the center’s ultimate goal is to help clients achieve lasting recovery and improve their overall quality of life.

faqs.q: Who owns Kelburn, and what is the new Kelburn?
faqs.a: Universal Ibogaine Inc., a company on the TSX Venture Exchange, bought Kelburn in October 2021 and named new leadership in January 2022. Spring flooding closed the centre in April 2022, and it reopened after renovations on October 17, 2022, which is most likely what reviewers mean by the new and improved Kelburn. The company now says its focus is a planned ibogaine clinical trial application to Health Canada.

Recovery.com estimated the 42-day program at $40,000 before the closure. Kelburn's own website gave no price, but it asked for a $5,000 deposit to hold a bed, with the balance due on arrival. Financing through iFinance was available up to $25,000.
Kelburn's inpatient program started at 42 days, according to its website. Medically assisted detox was part of those 42 days.

Yes, before it closed. Kelburn's website describes medically assisted detox with vital signs monitored 24/7 and medications such as benzodiazepines or methadone to manage withdrawal. Older listings, including the original version of this page, called it non-medical detox.
